props.gloss_en: 'in those days, when the king Ahasuerus sat [on his throne]' (Esther 1:2) -- the question's '!' presupposes this marks the start of his reign (Steinsaltz spells that out; the Hebrew leaves it implicit)
and after it is written: 'in the third year of his reign' (Esther 1:3)
Rava: what is 'when he sat'? after his mind was settled
Belshazzar calculated and erred
Ahasuerus erred in the calculation -- denied by Ahasuerus himself ('I will calculate and not err', 11b.6, 11b.12), asserted by the stam ('he too erred', 11b.13)
as it is written: 'for after seventy years are completed for Babylon I will remember you' (Jer 29:10)
and it is written: 'to complete for the desolations of Jerusalem seventy years' (Dan 9:2)
he [Belshazzar] counted: forty-five of Nebuchadnezzar, twenty-three of Evil-merodach and two of his own -- that is seventy
he [Belshazzar] took out the vessels of the Temple and used them
Nebuchadnezzar reigned forty-five years: eight and thirty-seven -- that is forty-five
as the Master said: they were exiled in the seventh, they were exiled in the eighth, they were exiled in the eighteenth, they were exiled in the nineteenth

'exiled in the seventh' -- of the conquest of Jehoiakim: the exile of Jehoiachin, which is the eighth of Nebuchadnezzar; 'in the eighteenth' -- of the conquest of Jehoiakim: the exile of Zedekiah, the nineteenth of Nebuchadnezzar
as the Master said: the first year he conquered Nineveh, the second he conquered Jehoiakim
and it is written: 'in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah ... Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year of his reign, lifted the head of Jehoiachin' (Jer 52:31)
and the twenty-three of Evil-merodach -- [known by] tradition (גמרא)
now surely they will no longer be redeemed
this is what Daniel said to him: 'you have lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven, and they brought the vessels of His house before you' (Dan 5:23)
and it is written: 'in that night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was slain' (Dan 5:30)
and it is written: 'and Darius the Mede received the kingdom, about sixty-two years old' (Dan 6:1)
is it written 'for the kingdom of Babylon'? 'for Babylon' is written. What is 'for Babylon'? for the exile of Babylon
how many are lacking? eight. He counted and put in their place one of Belshazzar, five of Darius and Cyrus, and two of his own -- that is seventy
once he saw that seventy were complete and they were not redeemed ... he took out the vessels of the Temple and used them
the Satan came and danced among them, and killed Vashti (the subject of 'killed' is the Hebrew's sequence; Steinsaltz reads it as Ahasuerus)
for he should have counted from the desolations of Jerusalem
why then is it written: 'then the work of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased' (Ezra 4:24)?
Rava: they were partial years
and there was yet another year for Babylon, and Darius arose and completed it
Rava: Daniel too erred in this calculation
as it is written: 'in the first year of his reign I, Daniel, understood in the books' (Dan 9:2); from his saying 'I understood' it follows that he had erred
Rava: [the seventy 'for Babylon' are] for mere remembrance

and this is what is written: 'thus says Cyrus king of Persia: all the kingdoms of the earth the Lord God of heaven has given me, and He has charged (פקד) me to build Him a house in Jerusalem' (Ezra 1:2)
what is that which is written: 'thus says the Lord to His anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held' (Isa 45:1)?
was Cyrus the anointed? rather, the Holy One said to the Messiah: I complain to you about Cyrus
I said: he will build My house and gather My exiles
and he said: 'whoever is among you of all His people ... let him go up' (Ezra 1:3)
